html:
A trade and defence pact signed in March 1261 at Nymphaeum, near Smyrna, between Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos of Nicaea and the Republic of Genoa.

Michael wanted a fleet to fight the Latin Empire in Constantinople and its protector Venice. Genoa, Venice's great trade rival, promised ships. In return Michael gave the Genoese the privileges Venice had enjoyed: trade free of customs duties, their own quarters in Byzantine ports, and access to the Black Sea, while Venice was to be shut out.

In the end Constantinople was retaken in July 1261 without Genoese help. But the treaty stood, and it changed the trade of the region for two centuries. In 1267 the Genoese got the suburb of Galata across the Golden Horn as their own colony, the Genoese colony at Galata, and built a chain of trading posts around the Black Sea such as Caffa in Crimea. Byzantium came to depend on Italian sea power it could not control.
sum: A trade and defence pact signed in March 1261 at Nymphaeum, near Smyrna, between Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos of Nicaea and the Republic of Genoa.
